_readme: THE SOURCE REGISTRY. One entry per data source, carrying the endpoint a reader would
have to hit and the EXACT filter values applied to it. It exists because an audit on
2026-08-17 found only 3 of 20 datasets published a source URL and none published its
industry or program codes, so the artifacts asserted reproducibility they did not
provide. A methodology box that names ‘BLS QCEW (the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages)’ without naming NAICS 3252 tells a
reader where to start and not what was done.
Every value below was extracted from the fetch scripts, not written from memory.
`script` is the file that hits the endpoint; run it and you get the same bytes.
`by_artifact` maps each published page to the sources it rests on, so PV.methodology()
can render the right subset without every derive script having to declare it. Adding a
page here is how it gets a reproduce block; tools/verify.mjs fails a page that has none.
PUBLIC CUT. This registry lists only the sources behind the analyses published in
this repository. The internal series has more pages and more sources; their
absence here is stated in the README rather than left to be discovered.

qcew.name: BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages

filters.NAICS codes: 10 (all industries), 31-33 (manufacturing), 325 (chemical manufacturing), 3252 (resin, synthetic rubber and fibers), 3255 (paint, coating and adhesive), 326 (plastics and rubber products), 3261 (plastics products), 3262 (rubber products)
filters.ownership: own_code 5 (private) carries every industry row; own_code 0 (total, all ownerships) exists only on industry 10. Those are not two interchangeable choices: an industry row at own_code 0 does not exist to be picked.
filters.aggregation: county area file: agglvl_code 70 is the all-ownership county total, 71 the county total by ownership, 74 NAICS sector, 75 NAICS 3-digit, 76 NAICS 4-digit, 77 5-digit, 78 6-digit. The US000 file uses 10, 11, 15, 16 and 18 for the same rungs. agglvl 50 to 58 are STATE levels and appear in no county file: 55 is three-digit, 56 four-digit, 57 five-digit and 58 six-digit.
filters.geography: county FIPS (the federal numeric code that identifies each county). The page’s own footprint, PIC-12, is 39007 Ashtabula, 39035 Cuyahoga, 39055 Geauga, 39085 Lake, 39093 Lorain, 39099 Mahoning, 39103 Medina, 39133 Portage, 39151 Stark, 39153 Summit, 39155 Trumbull, 39169 Wayne. The wider NEO-14 used by the vault pages is 39033 Crawford, 39035 Cuyahoga, 39055 Geauga, 39077 Huron, 39085 Lake, 39093 Lorain, 39099 Mahoning, 39103 Medina, 39133 Portage, 39139 Richland, 39151 Stark, 39153 Summit, 39157 Tuscarawas, 39169 Wayne. Both are defined once in footprints.py, which is a vendored copy of the pic-geo package.
filters.by_industry: the same census sliced the other way, one file per NAICS across every area, at https://data.bls.gov/cew/data/api/{year}/a/industry/{naics}.csv. The disclosure rates published on the sources page are the 2024 annual file for 326, own_code 5: county rows are agglvl 75, metropolitan rows agglvl 45, state rows agglvl 55.
filters.user_agent: This source is on data.bls.gov, which serves a scripted request with any User-Agent or none. The 403 is on www.bls.gov, which the two OEWS (the Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics survey) files use, and the warning is filed on those rather than here.
filters.note: PIC’s own measurement register is 3252 + 3255 + 326. NAICS 325 is context, not cluster: it contains pharmaceuticals and agricultural chemicals.
filters.provenance_page: fetch_provenance.py re-uses this source for one pull: 2016 annual, area 39000 which is the STATE of Ohio and not a county, own_code 5, industry 326+32521+325991 at agglvl 55/57/58, which are the state 3-, 5- and 6-digit levels. Those three agglvl codes belong to that state pull alone and return nothing from a county file.

qcew.terms: Public domain. BLS asks to be cited as the source: https://www.bls.gov/bls/linksite.htm

qwi.name: Census Quarterly Workforce Indicators, seasonally adjusted

filters.industry: 326 (plastics and rubber products manufacturing); 00 (all industries) as the benchmark on the talent demand chart
filters.note: EarnBeg is average monthly earnings of employees who also worked for the same employer in the prior quarter: stable jobs rather than new hires.

qwi.terms: Public domain. The Census Bureau asks to be cited as the source of the original data: https://www.census.gov/about/policies/citation.html

lodes.name: LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics, LODES8

filters.segment: JT00, meaning all jobs in all sectors. LODES origin-destination carries NO industry dimension, so this is the whole economy and never the polymer cluster.
filters.files: main (both ends in state) plus aux (work in state, home out of state). Omitting aux makes the region look artificially self-contained.
filters.geography: work end bounded to PIC-12 for the commute matrix; home end bounded to PIC-12 for the reciprocal; peer comparison reads twelve states’ main files
filters.note: Both ends are employer-reported addresses. The home end is a residence on file, not evidence anyone travelled.

lodes.terms: Public domain. The Census Bureau asks to be cited as the source of the original data: https://www.census.gov/about/policies/citation.html

ipeds.name: IPEDS Completions, via the Urban Institute Education Data API, with three years read from NCES directly
ipeds.agency: National Center for Education Statistics, served by the Urban Institute

filters.CIP-6 core: 143201 (polymer/plastics engineering), 400507 (polymer chemistry), 150607 (plastics and polymer engineering technology)
filters.CIP-6 adjacent: 141801 (materials engineering), 400510 (materials chemistry), 401001 (materials science), 141901 (mechanical engineering), 140701 (chemical engineering), 400501 (chemistry general), 151701 (energy systems technology)
filters.majornum: 1 only, so a double major is counted once
filters.race/sex: race=99 and sex=99 are the total rows; race=8 is nonresident alien. The two partitions are aggregated separately and never crossed; this endpoint does not offer the cross-tab at CIP-6.
filters.national benchmark: the same codes with no state filter, restricted to codes the footprint itself confers as a programme (which excludes 150607), since PIC-12’s entire history in it is two awards from one community college in one year
filters.note: Two earlier code entries did not exist and silently returned zero: 140320 (a transposition of 143201) and 143101 (materials science is in the 40 series, not 14). A core code returning zero across every year and institution is evidence of a bad code, not of no graduates.
filters.ipeds_cip: fetch_ipeds_cip.py adds institution × CIP × year (used by talent and occupations)
filters.year labels: The mirror’s year is the FALL of the academic year, so its 2023 is the NCES C2024_A file. That convention held through 2019 and again at 2023; in between, its 2020, 2021 and 2022 each served the collection year before the one they name, and C2023_A was served under no label at all. Those three years are therefore taken from the NCES completions files (https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/data/C{year}_A.zip, no key), by fetch_ipeds_nces.py; the correction table and its re-check are in _data/build/ipeds_mirror_fix.py. Degrees only: the recovered year also carries two postbaccalaureate certificates, which no other year of the series counts.

ipeds.attribution: Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) Completions, via Education Data Portal v. 0.26.1, Urban Institute, accessed 18 August 2026, https://educationdata.urban.org/documentation/, made available under the ODC (Open Data Commons) Attribution License.
ipeds.terms: The underlying IPEDS collection is a public-domain federal series, but the route this site uses is not the federal one. Everything served through the Urban Institute’s Education Data Portal is licensed to the user under the Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By) v1.0, which REQUIRES attribution and a citation naming the portal version and the access date: https://educationdata.urban.org/documentation/. Portal version 0.26.1 was released 2026-08-05 and was current at this site’s access date of 2026-08-18.

bea_rpp.name: BEA Regional Price Parities

filters.dataset: Regional, RPP by metropolitan statistical area
filters.base: a fixed national basket, US average = 100
filters.note: Published at METRO, which neither nests inside nor tiles PIC-12. Akron, Cleveland-Elyria and Youngstown-Warren each include territory the footprint excludes. Do not sum the three and call it PIC-12.

bea_rpp.terms: Public domain. BEA publishes citation guidelines: https://www.bea.gov/help/guidelines-for-citing-bea

fred.name: FRED producer price and commodity series
fred.agency: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

filters.series: WPU072 (PPI rubber and plastic products), WPU066 (PPI plastics resins and materials), WPU06 (PPI industrial chemicals), PCU326326 (PPI plastics and rubber products manufacturing), PCU325211325211 (PPI plastics material and resin manufacturing), WTISPLC (WTI crude oil spot)
filters.note: Producer price indexes, not consumer prices. Index levels, not dollars.
filters.run order: fetch_rest.py FIRST, then fetch_chain_prices.py. The second appends the feedstock and resin links to fred.json; running fetch_rest.py after it overwrites the file and silently drops them.

oews.name: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, metropolitan file

filters.geography: metropolitan area, carrying the same non-nesting caveat as BEA RPP
filters.note: One year only. This is a level, not a trend; the wage trend on the talent page comes from QWI instead.
filters.user_agent: www.bls.gov returns 403 to a scripted request with no User-Agent and to one impersonating a browser, and 200 to one naming a contact address. contact.py holds the single address this repository sends. data.bls.gov, which the QCEW (the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages) pulls use, serves any of them.

oews.terms: Public domain. BLS asks to be cited as the source: https://www.bls.gov/bls/linksite.htm

usaspending.name: USAspending federal contract and grant obligations

filters.method: POST with a JSON body, and the {category} path segment is required: naics and county are the two this site asks for. The endpoint without a category returns 404 to GET and to POST alike, which is what a reader who copies the stem alone will meet.
filters.NAICS: not sent to the API. A naics_codes filter returns 422, so the pull asks for the NAICS category over a county place-of-performance list and keeps 325* and 326* CLIENT-SIDE, in fetch_rest.py. University and research awards are invisible by construction either way: a university files under 61xxxx.
filters.paging: limit 100 per fiscal year per category, not paged. Anything past the hundredth result for a year is absent, and the file cannot tell you how much.
filters.geography: place of performance, a reported field on the award rather than an observation of where work happened
filters.note: Obligations are money legally committed, not cash spent.

usaspending.terms: Public domain federal spending data. USAspending states no additional licence.

usaspending_awards.name: USAspending award-level contract search

filters.method: POST with a JSON body; keyless. Filters: one spanning time_period 2018-10-01 to 2026-09-30 (FY2019-FY2026), place_of_performance_locations listing the 12 PIC-12 county codes, award_type_codes A-D (prime contracts; grants, loans and direct payments excluded), and naics_codes.
filters.NAICS: unlike the category endpoint, naics_codes IS sent to the API here, but it accepts only 2-, 4- or 6-digit codes: a 3-digit 325 returns 422 (‘only supported for lengths of 2, 4, and 6’). The pull sends the eleven 4-digit codes 3251-3259, 3261 and 3262, the same industry scope the category pull filters client-side.
filters.paging: limit 100, page walked while page_metadata.hasNext, to exhaustion: 6,630 rows over 67 pages at first fetch. A 40-page probe had 4,000 rows in hand and had NOT exhausted, so the fetcher asserts that floor and refuses to write a short pull. This is the register that closes the category pull’s own 100-row cap, and it must never inherit a cap of its own.
filters.basis: Award Amount is the award’s WHOLE-LIFE obligation, not the slice inside the window: an award running since 2014 that the window touches carries every dollar since 2014. A different basis from the per-fiscal-year spending_by_category sums, and the two are never summed; the fed-award-basis-never-summed claim holds both surfaces to saying so.
filters.geography: place of performance, a reported field on the award rather than an observation of where work happened

usaspending_awards.terms: Public domain federal spending data. USAspending states no additional licence.

filters.compiled: Merged from eight internal and public record sets: operational status reports, funding and award files, verified deck facts, and primary-press dates from the quote bank. 487 raw rows reduced to 104 dated events.
filters.publicOnly: Only events recorded as PUBLIC appear. Internal operational milestones, and the record of which dates slipped, are deliberately excluded; this is the public record, not the project’s whole history.
filters.forward_are_hollow: 18 of the 104 are future milestones and are drawn hollow, so a plan never reads as a fact.
filters.not_reproducible: Hand-compiled from documents rather than fetched from an API. Every event carries its own date and organisation; there is no script that regenerates this file, and pretending otherwise would be the opposite of what this registry is for.

heritage_register.name: NEO Polymer Wins register, heritage and discoveries collections
heritage_register.agency: Polymer Industry Cluster (internal register; only PROVEN rows and public sources travel)

filters.proven_only: Only rows the register’s INDEX labels PROVEN are emitted; the 5 CLAIMED rows are withheld as id + label + year only, with no wording.
filters.collections: heritage (what changed the region’s capacity) and discoveries (what was first understood here). The shipped, licensed, living and pic-era collections are a different tense and are not on this page.
filters.sources_travel: Only http(s) URLs and bibliographic lines travel; vault-path source references are stripped at build and counted (3).
filters.do_not_say_guard: Every emitted sentence is checked against the register’s own do-not-say list; a hit fails the build.
filters.wartime_tonnage: Four different measures exist in the sources and none is printed, which is the register’s standing rule.
filters.reproducibility: The register is internal; the builder (PIC-decks/tools/build-heritage-web.py) cannot be re-run from a public clone. The emitted data/heritage.json IS the published artifact, like the operating record; every row carries its public source URLs so each can be checked by hand.

oews_national.name: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, national file

filters.occupations: the SOC (the Standard Occupational Classification, the federal job-title code) set read from oews.json (26 codes); the metro pull defines the set
filters.dedupe: 51-2090 appears as broad and detailed with identical values; one row kept, detailed preferred
filters.note: all industries; the ‘#’ ceiling ($115/hr, $239,200/yr) and ‘*’ are both null, never zero
filters.user_agent: www.bls.gov returns 403 to a scripted request with no User-Agent and to one impersonating a browser, and 200 to one naming a contact address. contact.py holds the single address this repository sends. data.bls.gov, which the QCEW (the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages) pulls use, serves any of them.

oews_national.terms: Public domain. BLS asks to be cited as the source: https://www.bls.gov/bls/linksite.htm

onet_education.name: O*NET 30.3 database: Occupation Data, Job Zones, Job Zone Reference, Education, Education Categories
onet_education.agency: U.S. Department of Labor / Employment and Training Administration (CC BY 4.0; attribution printed on the page)

filters.element: 2.D.1 Required Level of Education, scale RL
filters.bins: 1-2 HS or less; 3-5 some college/associate; 6-7 bachelor’s; 8-12 graduate
filters.join: .00 variant preferred, else equal-weight mean of variants; broad SOC (the Standard Occupational Classification, the federal job-title code) 51-2090 = mean of five-char stem
filters.job_zone: 30.x reports zones 1 and 2 as one band keyed 2; a zone-1 row reads the merged reference row
filters.attribution: required on the page, printed in the education source line
filters.fetch: the .zip is the artifact and returns 200. The same path with the .zip trimmed off is a directory that returns 403 to every User-Agent tried, including a contact address, so a reader who shortens the URL to browse the files meets a wall rather than a listing.

nem.name: BLS Employment Projections, National Employment Matrix, industry to occupation

filters.industry: 326000 plastics and rubber products manufacturing (325000, 326100, 326200 also fetched)
filters.rows: Line Item detailed occupations only; Summary rows excluded
filters.geography: NATIONAL ONLY: no state or metro cut exists; any regional count built from it is a synthetic estimate under a stated assumption, and the sentence says so

nem.terms: Public domain. BLS asks to be cited as the source: https://www.bls.gov/bls/linksite.htm

odjfs.name: Ohio LMI long-term employment projections, 2022–2032
odjfs.agency: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services, Bureau of Labor Market Information

filters.geography: JobsOhio Northeast (18 counties, superset of PIC-12) and the four MSAs; Ashtabula and Wayne appear only in region and state figures
filters.row: one industry or one SOC (the Standard Occupational Classification, the federal job-title code) occupation × geography: 2022 base, 2032 projected, change, percent, annual openings split, median wage
filters.projection_not_forecast: a modelled path with no confidence band; historically under-calls turning points
filters.register_cannot_be_rebuilt: 3252 is published only inside bundle 3250A1 and 3255 only inside 3250A2; only 326/3261/3262 are clean
filters.access: ohiolmi.com returns 403 to a scripted request, browser User-Agent or not, so this one is a manual download: open the directory in a browser and save the spreadsheet. Verified 2026-08-29.

uspto.name: USPTO Open Data Portal, patent applications search
uspto.agency: United States Patent and Trademark Office

filters.method: POST with a JSON body carrying q and pagination; the count field of the reply is the figure, and no rows are read for a count.
filters.cpc: applicationMetaData.cpcClassificationBag:C08*, organic macromolecular compounds. One defensible definition of polymer, and a choice.
filters.basis: inventor correspondence address (applicationMetaData.inventorBag.correspondenceAddressBag): geographicRegionCode for the state, countryCode for the nation, cityName for a city; swap inventorBag for applicantBag for the ownership basis, which gives 3,948 all-time against the inventor basis’s 8,854. The year filter is applicationMetaData.filingDate:[YYYY-01-01 TO YYYY-12-31], and the all-technology series is the same query with the CPC clause removed.
filters.lag: an application publishes about eighteen months after filing, so the newest filing years are undercounted by construction and always look like a collapse. Years after 2023 are flagged incomplete rather than dropped.
filters.zero: a genuine zero arrives as HTTP 404 whose body reads No matching records. The fetch accepts that as 0 only when the body says so; any other 404 fails loudly, because a failed request silently becoming a zero is the suppression trap one endpoint over.
filters.dead_routes: PatentsView (search.patentsview.org) shut down 2026-03-20, and Patent Public Search answered every query with a 500 when tried on 2026-08-30. Both were candidate routes; neither is callable.
filters.worldwide_trap: a count with NO country filter is worldwide filings at the USPTO and reads flat across a window in which American polymer filings fell 22 percent, because foreign-origin filings filled the hole. The first version of the patents page made exactly this error and a replication reviewer caught it before publication: filter countryCode or say you did not.

uspto.terms: Public domain United States government work.

ipeds_programs_census.name: IPEDS completions by 6-digit CIP, 1991-2023 (the polymer-programs-db census)
ipeds_programs_census.agency: National Center for Education Statistics, via the Urban Institute Education Data API

filters.polymer CIP codes: 14.3201 Polymer/Plastics Engineering; 40.0507 Polymer Chemistry; 15.0607 Plastics and Polymer Engineering Technology
filters.years: 1991-2023 (2024 returns HTTP 500 from the API and is probed on every build)
filters.majors: first majors only from 2000; the distinction does not exist before 2000 and filtering earlier years on it silently returns zero rows
filters.award levels: certificate levels canonicalised across the 2020 IPEDS renumbering (1->31, 2/3->32, 5/6->33) before any counting
filters.census build: sibling checkout polymer-programs-db: fetch_ipeds_national.py -> raw_ipeds_national.json, build_db.py -> programs.sqlite; derive_programs.py reads the sqlite and cross-checks every published number

ipeds_directory.name: IPEDS institutional directory (coordinates and identity)
ipeds_directory.agency: National Center for Education Statistics, via the Urban Institute Education Data API

filters.lookup: per-unitid, year 2023 with fallback to the institution’s last active year
filters.trap: a year’s directory omits institutions that closed before it, and the latitude/longitude fields begin in 2009: seven pre-2009 closures are placed at hand city centroids, stated per-dot
filters.projection: points and basemap pre-projected at build time into the us-atlas AlbersUSA frame (975x610, scale 1300, translate 487.5/305): NOT d3 defaults

ipeds_control_cips.name: The same IPEDS pull for six peer technician CIPs (the control, on two populations)
ipeds_control_cips.agency: National Center for Education Statistics, via the Urban Institute Education Data API

filters.control CIP codes: 48.0508 Welding; 48.0501 Machine Tool; 15.0613 Manufacturing Eng Tech; 47.0303 Industrial Mechanics and Maintenance; 15.0303 Electrical/Electronic Eng Tech; 15.0805 Mechanical Eng Tech
filters.rule: identical to the polymer census: substantive = more than 10 lifetime completions, active = a completion in 2023, same years, same award-level canonicalisation
filters.control build: sibling checkout polymer-programs-db: fetch_control_cips.py -> control_cips.json, read by derive_programs.py, for the survival control. The base-rate control is pulled in this repository by fetch_ipeds_control_baserate.py, keyless, and will not write until it reproduces the published 48% from the live API
filters.two populations: the SURVIVAL control counts substantive programs only (6,648 ever, 3,185 still, 48%); the BASE-RATE control counts every start with the size threshold OFF (8,736 ever, 23% at ten or fewer completions, 19% both tiny and brief), because thresholding on size would discard the population a start-and-fail rate is about. The two counts are of the same six trades under two different rules and must never be quoted against each other

scorecard_fos_polymer.name: College Scorecard field-of-study earnings and debt, polymer engineering

filters.vintages: latest = 2020 cohorts for 1-year earnings, 2022 file for 4-year earnings, 2019 file for debt; any ratio across them mixes cohorts
filters.dedupe: census_match=1 only - the Scorecard attaches Penn State Behrend’s values to Main Campus too, and the duplicate reads as a sixth institution
filters.suppression: 84% of cells are privacy-suppressed and suppression tracks program size; the five published institutions are the biggest programs, not a sample
filters.acquisition: sibling checkout polymer-programs-db/incoming/college-scorecard: fetch_scorecard.py -> scorecard_fos_polymer_tidy.csv, read by derive_programs.py

filters.institutions: I110152177 (University of Akron), I58956616 (Case Western Reserve University)
filters.subject bound: topics.subfield.id:2507, ‘Polymers and Plastics’. A CLASSIFICATION, not a keyword.
filters.reported alongside: subfield 2502 ‘Biomaterials’, counted separately and never merged in
filters.taxonomy source: subfield ids confirmed against s3://openalex/data/jsonl/subfields, not inferred from documentation
filters.note: An earlier bound matched the full-text word ‘polymer’ and returned 4,037 works, four of whose five largest partners were hospitals. The classification returns 1,448. Author position uses is_corresponding, not first author, because in this field the first author is normally the graduate student.
filters.one script deliberately omitted: fetch_openalex.py hits this same endpoint but is still on the old keyword bound and returns the superseded 4,037 figure. No published page reads its output, so it is left out rather than handing a reader a script that reproduces the wrong number. Audited 2026-08-17.

filters.scope: every award to either university since 2012-01-01
filters.joint detection: two ways: one award naming investigators at both institutions by email domain, and NSF’s ‘Collaborative Research’ mechanism, which issues a separate award per institution under an identical title
filters.note: Only awards NSF itself labels ‘Collaborative Research’ are counted as joint. Matching on shared title alone booked ‘Graduate Research Fellowship Program’: an institutional block grant every university receives separately, as a $1.1M joint project.

NOT public and NOT reproducible by a reader. Company self-descriptions are quoted as written and are never rewritten: a company that writes ‘injection moulding’ said that. Any public release of these records is gated on member consent (Linear POL-1011).

filters.unit: ESTABLISHMENTS: one physical site, not one company. A firm with three plants is three establishments.
filters.note: Census and PIC define a firm differently, so a coverage ratio can exceed 100 percent without the county being fully covered.

_why: THE SIX NUMBERS THE RECIPE IS BUILT ON, read off the two files the recipe tells a
reader to download, so the guide can print the arithmetic AND the arithmetic it is not.
They are here rather than derived from a shipped page file because no page here ships
the two PRIVATE all-industry totals: the site never divides by them. A reader who
follows the intuitive same-ownership rule does, lands on a different number, and is
entitled to be told which is which instead of assuming they made a mistake.
THEY ARE NOT TRUSTED. derive_sources.py recomputes BLS's own basis from these six
values and FAILS THE BUILD unless it reproduces the location quotient the pay page
publishes for the same cell to within 0.005. If a refetch moves that cell and nobody
moves these, the build stops rather than teaching a recipe that no longer lands.
worked_example.rows: local: own_code 5 industry 326 agglvl 75; own_code 0 industry 10 agglvl 70; own_code 5 industry 10 agglvl 71. national (US000): own_code 5 industry 326 agglvl 15; own_code 0 industry 10 agglvl 10; own_code 5 industry 10 agglvl 11.

ownership_self_check._what: The county file proves its own denominator. Each ownership TOTAL row carries a location quotient of its own, and on a same-ownership basis every one of them would be exactly 1.00 by construction. They are not.

by_industry_vintage._what: The disclosure chart is a VINTAGE, and the page has to say which one or a reader who pulls the newest year reads a normal year-on-year change as a discrepancy in our arithmetic. The published year is checked against the peers page's own shipped counts at build time; the comparison year is recorded here with the date it was read.
